column2: Tola follows Abimelech as Israel's deliverer; Puah, the father's-brother relationship, Issachar, Samaria and Ephraim's hill country remain as selected.
column3: The antecedent of his in the compressed genealogy is not resolved by the English; no familiar alternate grandfather is inserted.

column2: The twenty-three-year judgeship precedes Tola's death and burial in Samaria; both selected notices remain.
Jair is Gileadite and judges twenty-two years after Tola; the distinct duration is preserved.
The selected thirty-two occurs for sons, mounts and cities; all three counts and Jair's Settlements remain, without harmonizing to thirty.
column3: Young donkeys specifies the contextual kind of poloi; the Greek noun itself is a broader young-animal term.

column2: Jair dies and is buried in Rammo; the selected site is retained.
Again represents the renewed-action construction; the six worship objects remain in order, followed by both abandoning the Lord and not serving Him.
The Lord's anger and sale into the hands of foreigners and Ammonites remain His actions; greatly conveys the intensified anger construction.
Both weakening and crushing remain, together with the difficult in-that-year/eighteen-years sequence and the eastern Amorite-Gilead location.
column3: The chronology is left visible rather than silently reconstructed; the dash is an English reading aid, not a textual solution.

column2: The Ammonites cross the Jordan and fight also against Judah, Benjamin and Ephraim; Israel's severe distress follows.
The confession is direct singular address to God, hence Thee; abandoning our God and serving the Baalim both explain the sin.
The negative question begins an oppressor list completed in verse 12; Egypt, Amorites, Ammon, Moab and foreigners are retained here.
Sidonians, Midian and Amalek complete the question; Israel's cry and the Lord's rescue follow as distinct clauses.
Israel's abandonment and service of other gods explain the refusal of further rescue; no more represents the negative renewed-action construction.
Both commands, going and crying, lead to the taunt that the gods chosen for themselves should save them in distress.
Propose Do Thou to represent the emphatic divine-address subject su, and but for plen, preserving the plea after unconditional submission rather than suggesting an exclusive demand.
column3: Do Thou is deliberate established divine-address English; the remaining all-whatever construction is carried by whatever, not an extra all.

column2: Removing foreign gods and worshiping the Lord do not erase the selected negative statement that He was not pleased; His response to Israel's distress remains a separate clause.
column3: Grew weary for oligopsycheo is provisional: became discouraged or fainthearted requires lexical assessment. No familiar compassion-only reading replaces this selected form.

column2: Ammon's ascent and camp at Gilead contrast with Israel's departure and camp at Mizpah; the distinct movements remain.
Gilead's rulers ask one another who will begin the fight, and promise that person headship over all inhabitants; begin is not dropped.
Jephthah's strength, his mother's designation as a harlot and her bearing him to Gilead remain; the mother is the subject of bore.
Gilead's wife's sons expel Jephthah after growing up and deny inheritance because of his mother; courtesan preserves the differing selected designation hetaira.
column3: The relation between porne in verse 1 and hetaira here needs lexical review; no claim of two different professions is made.

column2: Flight from his brothers leads to Tob and a following of men of little means who go out with him; no raiding action is supplied.
column3: Men of little means for litoi is contextual and provisional; their exact social characterization remains open.

column2: After some days introduces renewed Ammonite conflict without inventing a more precise elapsed time.
The elders travel to obtain Jephthah during the fighting; the sentence continues into their invitation in verse 6.
Come and become our leader is linked to their proposed collective fight; so that gives the invitation's contextual purpose.
Jephthah charges the elders with hatred, expulsion from his father's house and dismissal from them; the three actions and distress question remain.
Not so is the elders' response, followed by accompanying them, fighting and headship over all Gilead; no apology is inserted.
His return and the Lord's delivery of Ammon are the conditions for Jephthah's headship; the selected final statement remains declarative.
Propose The Lord shall be for the future estai instead of May the Lord be; the elders invoke the Lord as the One hearing between them and give an oath-like assurance.
column3: Surely we will do represents the negative conditional oath formula ei me; it does not render a simple unqualified affirmative token-for-token.

column2: The elders establish Jephthah as both head and leader; he speaks all his words before the Lord at Mizpah.
The what-is-there-between-us idiom introduces a challenge about the king's coming to fight in Jephthah's land; ordinary human you remains.
The king claims land from Arnon to Jabbok and Jordan, then demands restore them in peace; the shift from singular land to plural autas remains visible.
column3: The plural object's exact referents are not supplied as cities or territories without evidence.

column2: The messengers first return to Jephthah, who then sends messengers; the full selected return notice is preserved without adding again.
Jephthah denies taking either Moab's or Ammon's land; English or operates under the shared negative and the sentence continues into verse 16.
The departure from Egypt is plural in they, then Israel travels by the wilderness to the Red Sea and Kadesh; the selected number shift remains.
Edom does not listen and Moab is unwilling; the two refusals and Israel's remaining at Kadesh stay distinct.
Israel circles both Edom and Moab and reaches Moab's east, then they camp beyond Arnon without entering Moab because it is the boundary.
The request goes to Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon; passing to my place remains the stated destination rather than a supplied conquest objective.
Sihon refuses passage, gathers all his people and fights from Jahaz; unwillingness is not rewritten as mistrust.
The Lord hands over Sihon and all his people, and Israel strikes and inherits; explicit Israel in the middle clause clarifies the contextual human subject.
column3: The subject of the unexpressed he-struck verb is inferred from narrative context, not separately named in that Greek clause.

column2: The full territory has four bounds in two pairs: Arnon/Jabbok and wilderness/Jordan; no boundary is omitted.
The Lord removes the Amorite before His people; Jephthah challenges the opponent's proposed inheritance for himself.
column3: English it takes the object as the disputed territory, while Greek auton is masculine and recalls the collective Amorite; the metonymic referent needs review.

column2: The comparison appeals to Chemosh's allotment and the Lord's allotment; it stays Jephthah's argument, without added theological evaluation.
The comparison with Balak son of Zippor and both fighting questions remain; ever voices the rhetorical force of the emphatic constructions.
column3: Ever is contextual interrogative emphasis, not a separate Greek temporal word; a closer form without it remains available.

column2: The house of Israel, Heshbon, Jazer, dependent towns, Jordan cities and three hundred years remain; third-person they is not changed to second-person you.
column3: The subjects and objects of did they not rescue them are not explicit; the inherited question preserves the ambiguity.

column2: Jephthah denies his own wrong, accuses the king's warfare and asks the judging Lord to judge today between Israel and Ammon; the repeated judicial language remains.
Both did-not-listen clauses are preserved, with the second specifying the words Jephthah sent; repetition is not edited away.
The Lord's Spirit comes upon Jephthah before his transit through Gilead, Manasseh and the repeated Gilead Watchpost; the place expression is not silently harmonized to Mizpah.
The vowed-a-vow repetition and emphatic delivery condition remain; Thou wilt is direct singular address to the Lord.
Whoever reflects the personal relative, and the conjunction before I will offer remains and; the vow expressly names a whole burnt offering.
column3: No or, alternative dedication or later interpretive outcome is inserted. That one renders the anaphoric auton without prespecifying the arriving person's gender in English.

column2: Jephthah crosses to fight, and the Lord delivers the Ammonites into his hand; military action and divine agency remain distinct.
Aroer, Semoith, twenty cities and Abel of the Vineyards remain, followed by the great blow and Ammon's shame before Israel.
Look carries the presentative particle; his daughter approaches with tambourines and dances, his only beloved child with neither another son nor daughter.
Jephthah tears his garments and voices the foot-entanglement and eye-thorn images; the concerning-you phrase and inability to turn back remain.
column3: Entangled my feet is an image-bearing rendering of the compound impediment verb, not a claim that the daughter physically restrained him.

column2: The daughter's conditional response links his spoken vow concerning her to what she asks him to do, and cites the Lord's vengeance upon Ammon.
The request is two months to descend upon the mountains and weep over virginity with companions; the selected downward movement is retained.
column3: Go down compresses go-and-descend into one English movement phrase; the geographical oddity is not repaired by changing down to up.

column2: The father grants departure for two months; the daughter and companions go, but the selected weeping verb is singular and remains she wept.
Jephthah fulfills the vow after two months; the narrator adds that she had not known a man and introduces an ordinance, without an expanded account of fulfillment.
column3: The text's vow and fulfillment must be read together without importing a celibacy-only resolution or adding details of death absent from this unit.

column2: Year by year conveys the recurring-day idiom, with four days in each year and daughters going together to lament; lament is not changed to a friendly visit.
